## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e3ce4aa7c8a0f500a443c52bbda0faa9c8c2846a`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`, run in a throwaway worktree of the head (`/tmp/claude-0/seat3/wt-31181`, since removed), because the brief asks for the token reading from the repo's own ratchet (exit 0; `objectstack-platform/SKILL.md 6011 / 6011 (+0)`). In the same worktree I also ran `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 31181` (exit 3, GOVERNED, Tier H). Main-side bytes were taken by hand (`git show origin/main:<file> | wc -c`, minus the 20-byte release-stamp line, then ceil(bytes/4)).
Scope: the 3 files of `git diff origin/main...refs/seat3/pr-31181` (merge base `21c1f7485`; content commit `221a7ff23` plus the merge `e3ce4aa7c` of `origin/main` `21c1f7485`): .changeset/skills-platform-always-on-requires.md, skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-platform/evals/config-plugins-ops.json. `origin/main` has since moved to `eb68b9814`; none of the code sites below differ between `21c1f7485` and `eb68b9814`. Cited code read: packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts (`PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS` L31-84, `PLATFORM_ALWAYS_ON_CAPABILITIES` L350-393), packages/core/src/capability-composition.ts (`resolveServedCapabilities` L115-140, `NEEDS_JOB_AND_QUEUE` L86), packages/core/src/capability-providers.ts (`CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` L64-236), packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts (L2971-3011 host defaults and the resolver call; `Serve.CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` L2101; `resolverMounted` L5144), packages/types/src/env.ts (`isMcpServerEnabled` L633), packages/cli/package.json (the eleven slate provider packages), packages/objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts (`describeMissingOwnershipQueueService` L703) and packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (`assertOwnershipQueueServicePresent` L677), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts (L1064 `skipped: true`), scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs.

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #31130 (body; triage 6707823515; claim 6709315868), the PR body (identical to /mnt/project-files/card-31130/body-v1.md apart from the attribution comment), the order at /mnt/project-files/skills-seat3/order-31130.md, the gate records gates-221a7ff2.txt and gates-e3ce4aa7-recheck.txt (all exit 0), preclaim.md, the commit, the net diff, and the seat's mid-flight rulings Q1, Q2 and the host-default ruling. Each taught fact was checked against code:

- **Item 1, the always-on list.** TRUE.
  - The ° marks sit on exactly `queue`, `job`, `cache`, `settings`, `email`, `storage`, `sms`, `sharing`, `messaging`, `analytics`, `package-registry`. That is `PLATFORM_ALWAYS_ON_CAPABILITIES`, no more and no less. The changeset lists the same eleven.
  - "`--preset minimal` drops exactly those" holds. `resolveServedCapabilities` skips the slate when `preset === 'minimal'` and skips nothing else. Host defaults are appended before that check, so minimal keeps them.
  - Two tokens can come back under minimal. `auth` appends `email` (L126), and that is now taught ("even under `--preset minimal`"). `email`, `approvals` or `auth` also pull `job` and `queue` to the front (L135-138). That is not taught. See N1.
  - "Every boot mounts them, listed or not" holds for `os serve`. Every slate token has a `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` row, including `package-registry` at L174. `packages/cli/package.json` depends on all eleven provider packages. A slate token that cannot be built is logged and skipped, which matches "Declaring is a demand".
  - No count in prose. The new lead names no number. "Five rules" is old text, and the bullet count is still five.
  - Host defaults (`mcp` unless `OS_MCP_SERVER_ENABLED` is off; `pinyin-search` for a `zh-*` locale) are not taught. The seat's ruling allows this, and the body lists it under other sites. See S3.
- **Item 2, table rows.** TRUE.
  - All 22 `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` keys have a row. Add the 5 tier tokens and 3 enterprise/cloud tokens in the bullets below the table, and that is all 30 entries of `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS`. No phantom row and no missing row.
  - Every row names the registry package. `service-` + token for analytics, cache, storage, queue, job, messaging, realtime, settings, sms, push. `plugin-` + token for audit, email, sharing, approvals, webhooks. `service-package` for both marketplace and package-registry.
  - Unmarked rows are correct: `realtime`, `push`, `marketplace`, `audit`, `approvals`, `webhooks`, `automation`, `mailbox`, `pinyin-search`, `mcp`, `triggers`. Code comments confirm `push` and `mailbox` are "requested, never always-on".
  - The ° sits outside the backticks, so liveness parsing of the token spans is unchanged. The gate record shows `check:skill-identifier-liveness` exit 0.
- **Item 3, the triggers/job bullet (Q2).** TRUE.
  - `triggers` mounts `trigger-record-change` plus `trigger-schedule` and `TimeRelativeTriggerPlugin`. The schedule and time-relative plugins run on the job service (provider comment L114-131).
  - On a default boot `job` is on the slate. Under minimal it is absent unless listed, or unless `email` / `approvals` / `auth` pulls it in (N1). The advice is safe, and the scope is right.
- **Item 4, deletions that pay the budget.** Each cut fact has a home.
  - Tier-gated ", the other three through their tier blocks". The fact is that `i18n` / `ui` / `auth` open their own tier blocks. The home is the same bullet: "dedicated blocks in `serve.ts` `run()` open their tier instead", over all five tokens.
  - `auth` "so the CLI appends `email` whenever `auth` is required". The facts are that it is automatic and that `auth` triggers it. The home is the bullet head "`auth` implies `email`". The "appended, so best-effort" nuance lives in "Declaring is a demand" ("one the platform auto-injects … stays best-effort").
  - `automation` "they have nowhere to register and". This was a restatement. The home is the same sentence: "connector executors register their provider factories with it".
  - triggers "autolaunched" and "without `job`". The home is the head "pair `triggers` with `job`" plus "scheduled flows stay silent".
  - Lead "and … is what". Wording only.
  - Ratchet: 24045 → 24061 bytes, so 6007 → 6011 against a ceiling of 6011. The script exits 0. `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is unchanged against `origin/main`, and no ceiling moved. No re-wrap was used to save bytes. The `automation` and `triggers` bullets keep their line counts. The lead grew a line, and its long third line was left unwrapped (N3).
  - The net +4 is drawn from headroom, not paid by deletion. See S2.
- **Item 5, evals.** The JSON parses. Ids run 1-20 with no gaps.
  - Case 3 (Q1): TRUE. `triggers` arms the start bindings. `job` and `messaging` are on the slate. Under minimal, notify returns `{ delivered: 0, failed: 0, skipped: true }` without messaging (notify-node.ts L1064). `job` / `messaging` are gone from `must_contain`, and the always-on plus `--preset minimal` caveat is stated. But one `must_not_contain` fails a careful answer. See S1.
  - Case 20: TRUE. `storage` and `settings` are on the slate. Listing one is harmless, because the CLI ships both providers. Only minimal drops them. `automation` and `mailbox` are correct examples of tokens that mount only when listed.
  - Sweep for the old opt-in claim: case 9 only. Its `expected_output` says "plus `'sharing'` in `requires` … else the boot is refused", and `must_contain` has `'sharing'`. The refusal (`describeMissingOwnershipQueueService`) fires only when the `ownership-queue` service is unregistered. `sharing` is on the slate, and case 9's own prompt names a default boot (`requires: ['automation', 'triggers']`). So the case teaches "a service is absent unless listed", which is the false claim the card names (body: "believes a service is absent unless listed (wrong)"). It is the same defect Q1 fixed in case 3. My judgment: case 9 is inside the card's ask in substance, but outside the claim's "one case" surface. It moves with M1. Cases 7 and 8 mention `email` only as a field.
- **Item 6, process.** Checked.
  - The changeset carries `'@objectstack/skills': patch`. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in the changeset (L7-8) and the body (L9-10).
  - The body has `Fixes #31130` (L7). It carries the model waiver, which names no model ("the project's default model"). No model identifier appears in the body, diff or commits. The trailers are `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` and `Claude-Session:`.
  - Only claimed files are touched.
  - The merge is clean. `git diff <main parent> e3ce4aa7c` shows only the three files, and `git show --cc` has no conflict hunks.
  - Tier: `check-governed-merges --pr 31181` exits 3: GOVERNED, Tier H, `skills/**` ×2. The changeset is off the register. The size is +45 / −19, under 3000.
- **Item 7, other sites.** Confirmed for filing below (③). L55-56 is not merely another site. See M1.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` is right. Only skill prose and an eval fixture change, and `@objectstack/skills` ships both. No platform behaviour moves, so `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Claim.** All three paths are inside claim 6709315868. The SKILL.md edits sit in § `### requires:` and nowhere else. The eval edits are case 3 (Q1) and the new case 20 ("optional" under Q1). No breach.
- **Ratchet script.** Unchanged. Standing ruling 6513306068 was not used.
- **Tier.** GOVERNED, Tier H. Landing needs the maintainer's merge or an APPROVED review from `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`, and the body's 「需要你做的」 says so. The PR is a draft, `mergeable_state` blocked. Labels: documentation, size/s, tooling.
- **Interplay.** The body names #31115 item 2 and the re-read rule.
- **Other sites outside the claim, confirmed for filing.**
  1. SKILL.md L55-56 "(`sharing` in `requires`): … refused at boot", plus eval case 9. Confirmed false on a default boot (see ① item 5). This one is promoted to M1, because the PR makes the page contradict itself.
  2. objectstack-automation SKILL.md § Prerequisite table (L341-350). The `job`, `queue` and `messaging` rows give "Absent ⇒" outcomes ("scheduled flows never launch", "503", "silent: success with `skipped: true`"). All three are on the slate, so those outcomes happen only under minimal. Same teaching at references/examples-flows.md L132 ("plus `'job'`") and references/integration-recipes.md L62 (`requires: ['automation', 'triggers', 'job']`). Confirmed.
  3. Host defaults. `mcp` mounts unless `OS_MCP_SERVER_ENABLED` is `0` / `false` / `off` / `no` (`isMcpServerEnabled` returns true when unset). `pinyin-search` mounts for a `zh-*` locale. Both apply under every preset, minimal included, and neither is taught. Confirmed.
  4. The platform-capabilities.ts jsdoc on `'package-registry'` (L385-392) says the token is "inert" under `objectstack serve` because the registry keys only `marketplace`. That is stale: core's `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` keys `package-registry` at L174, and `Serve.CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` is that table (serve.ts L2101). Confirmed.

### ④ Design judgment

- **must-fix M1: the page now contradicts itself on `sharing`.**
  - The new lead says `sharing`° is always-on: "every boot mounts them, listed or not".
  - L55-56, in the same SKILL.md, still says `queues` / `assignmentRules` need the service "(`sharing` in `requires`): a stack declaring either without it is refused at boot".
  - So one page says both "X is always on" and "list X or boot is refused". Code sides with the lead on a default boot. The refusal tests only whether `ownership-queue` is registered, and the slate registers it. L55-56 is true only under `--preset minimal`.
  - Before this PR both sentences were wrong in the same direction. The PR makes one of them right, which exposes the other.
  - The fix is a deletion and fits the claim's "same-file deletions" clause. Drop " (`sharing` in `requires`)" so the line reads "…`@objectstack/plugin-sharing` registers: a stack declaring either without it is refused at boot." That is true on every preset, and the lead already covers minimal. It saves 26 bytes, bringing the file to about 6004 / 6011, so it also settles S2.
  - Eval case 9 must move with it. Its `expected_output` should say `sharing` is always-on and is listed only under `--preset minimal`. Its `must_contain` should be `sharing`, not `'sharing'`. That is a second corrected case beyond the claim's "one case", so it needs a seat ruling of the same kind as Q1, or the seat files it with the L55-56 report.
- **should-fix S1: case 3's new `must_not_contain` fails the answer the case asks for.** The expected output tells the reader to list `job` and `messaging` under `--preset minimal`. A careful answer writes that line as `requires: ['automation', 'triggers', 'job', 'messaging']`, which contains the banned `'triggers', 'job', 'messaging'`. Drop the entry. The `always-on` and `--preset minimal` musts already rule out the old answer.
- **should-fix S2: the body overstates how growth was paid.** 「增长全部用同节删除支付」 and "The growth … is paid by deletions in the same section" are not quite right. Gross growth was partly paid, and the net +4 (6007 → 6011) came from existing headroom. The script accepts that, and the order's "6011/6011 on main" was a misreading (main is 6007). Correct the sentence, or take M1's deletion, which makes the net change negative.
- **should-fix S3: the lead's "Every other service plugin is opt-in" is still false for `mcp` and `pinyin-search`.** Both mount by host default under every preset. The seat ruled this goes under other sites unless cheap, and the body files it (other site 3). I record it so the filing names this sentence as the defect. After M1 frees about 7 tokens, "on by default unless `OS_MCP_SERVER_ENABLED` is off" on the `mcp` row may fit. That is the seat's call.
- **nit N1: under minimal, `email`, `approvals` or `auth` pulls `job` and `queue` back in** (`NEEDS_JOB_AND_QUEUE`). So "scheduled flows stay silent" does not hold for a minimal stack that lists `auth`. The advice to pair is still safe. No change needed at zero headroom. Mention it in the filing for other site 2.
- **nit N2: `must_contain: "always-on"` (cases 3 and 20) is spelling-sensitive.** A correct answer saying "always on" or "on the always-on slate" without the hyphen fails. Case 20's `must_not_contain: "requires: ['storage', 'settings']"` could, rarely, fail an answer that shows the minimal-preset line. Accept the risk, or loosen it.
- **nit N3: the lead's third line runs about 105 characters.** The author left it unwrapped to avoid a re-wrap, which is the right instinct. A re-flow at equal line count costs no bytes, so it is optional.
- **nit N4: commit 221a7ff23's message says it scopes "the auth/email and triggers/job rules" to minimal.** The auth/email rule is not scoped; it now says "even under". The commit is pushed and must not be rewritten, so this is for the record only.
- **Check-runs on this head**, read 2026-11-07T16:24Z: 38 runs, 20 success, 13 skipped, 5 in progress, 0 failed.

Verdict: FAIL
